harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a locked-password opsbot account on node1 and node2, generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key as node2's opsbot authorized_key, and added an explicit Match User opsbot sshd block on both nodes forcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / AuthenticationMethods publickey. Verified opsbot can SSH key-only from node1 to node2 and that password auth is rejected on both nodes. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol on node1 and node2, confirming boot_id changes and full recovery of ssh.socket, the opsbot account/keys, the sshd Match block, and working end-to-end key-based SSH after both reboots.
actions_performed: Confirmed opsbot did not exist and inspected global sshd auth settings on node1/node2
Created opsbot user with locked password on node1 and node2 (useradd -m, passwd -l)
Generated ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1 (/home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519)
Installed opsbot's public key into node2 /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership/permissions
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-opsbot.conf Match User opsbot block on both nodes enforcing pubkey-only auth; validated with sshd -t
Generated missing sshd host keys (ssh-keygen -A) and created /run/sshd, then restarted ssh.socket on both nodes to apply config
Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH to opsbot@node2 via key with BatchMode (no password) and that password-only auth attempts are rejected with Permission denied (publickey) on both nodes
Captured baseline boot_id/uptime/service health on both nodes
Restarted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id/uptime, and verified opsbot account, keys, sshd config, and cross-node SSH still work
Restarted node2 via shutdown -r now, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id/uptime, and verified opsbot account, keys, sshd config, and cross-node SSH still work
Re-verified password auth is still rejected for opsbot on both nodes after both reboots

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Confirmed opsbot absent, then created with locked password on both nodes; id opsbot shows uid=1000 on each.

evidence.requirement: SSH key-based access from node1 opsbot to run commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: Generated ed25519 keypair on node1, installed public key into node2 opsbot authorized_keys, and successfully ran `whoami` as opsbot on node2 from node1 over SSH using only the key (BatchMode=yes).

evidence.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems (password auth disabled)
evidence.summary: Added Match User opsbot block (PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) on both nodes, validated with sshd -t, reloaded ssh.socket, and confirmed a password-only SSH attempt to opsbot on each node is rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'.
Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-..., uptime start 09:57:18, ssh.socket active, opsbot present with keys/known_hosts intact.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Issued shutdown -r now (ack via connection reset), polled until exec worked again showing new boot_id 37dd6d9c-... and new uptime start 09:59:15, then verified ssh.socket active, opsbot account/keys intact, sshd Match block intact, and key-based SSH to node2 opsbot still succeeds.
Captured boot_id 29011044-..., uptime start 09:57:17, ssh.socket active, opsbot present with authorized_keys intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Issued shutdown -r now (ack via connection reset), polled until exec worked again showing new boot_id 8612462b-... and new uptime start 09:59:30, then verified ssh.socket active, opsbot account/keys/sshd Match block intact, and confirmed from node1 that key-based SSH to node2 opsbot still succeeds while password-only auth is still rejected.

Verified opsbot can SSH key-only from node1 to node2 and that password auth is rejected on both nodes. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol on node1 and node2, confirming boot_id changes and full recovery of ssh.socket, the opsbot account/keys, the sshd Match block, and working end-to-end key-based SSH after both reboots.
